A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffusionBlocks work despite retitling and substantial expansion. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet generation results, LM1B language-generation results, and partitioning, overlap, and block-count ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification and generation experiments across several architectures, including CIFAR-100, image generation, text8, LM1B, and OpenWebText, with additional analyses in Tables 6–9.

M1.justification: The continuous-noise block-training core remains, but v2 introduces substantive adaptations: noisy label embeddings for ViT classification, masking-schedule partitioning for discrete diffusion, and single-pass denoising training of recurrent-depth networks without block partitioning. Sections 5.1, 5.3, and 5.5 and Appendices A/C describe these procedural extensions; the rewritten conversion recipe also clarifies existing components.

E1.justification: v2 adds CIFAR-100 image classification, text8 character modeling with masked diffusion, and OpenWebText language generation. CIFAR-10 and ImageNet generation and LM1B language generation remain. These additions expand actual task and data coverage beyond v1's image generation and LM1B experiments.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's end-to-end baselines, v2 evaluates ViT and Forward-Forward for classification, MD4 for masked language modeling, Huginn for recurrent-depth generation, and NoProp-DT, NoProp-CT, NoProp-FM, and their associated Backprop comparator on CIFAR-100. These methods appear in reported comparisons, not merely citations. The DiT end-to-end comparator remains.

E3.justification: Main image experiments change from four blocks with overlap 0.1 to three with overlap 0.05; ImageNet also changes VAE checkpoint and learning rate from 1e-4 to 5e-5. Autoregressive text generation changes from 50 to four diffusion steps and adds teacher-model generative perplexity. New protocols include the 10% OpenWebText holdout and Huginn's unequal 15-versus-five-epoch training budgets. These are reported setting changes, not evidence that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 expands the partitioning study to four layer allocations, adds an LM1B block-count sweep, and compares NoProp variants on their CNN architecture to examine continuous-time block independence. The CIFAR-10 block-count analysis remains with revised settings. Conversely, v1's five-setting overlap-sensitivity sweep is removed, although overlap remains part of the method.

E5.justification: Both experimental appendices report the minimum of three FID evaluations. Neither supplies training-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The three evaluations do not establish three independent training runs, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and added. CIFAR-10 baseline/DiffusionBlocks FID changes from 41.87/41.39 in v1 Table 1 to 39.83/37.20 in v2 Table 2; LM1B MAUVE changes from 0.595/0.779 to 0.50/0.71. These are results under revised settings, not same-setting gains or losses. New classification, text8, Huginn, and OpenWebText results appear; OpenWebText MAUVE favors AR, 0.85 versus 0.82. Ablation values change, and v1's generated examples disappear.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix C adds a masked-diffusion objective and derives its decomposition into independent block losses, with boundaries defined by equal decrements of the unmasking probability. This extends the mathematical treatment beyond v1's continuous VE formulation. Section 3.1 also explicitly assumes dimension-preserving token maps. The shared residual/Euler argument is largely retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution broadens from superior image/text generation to a systematic conversion framework spanning classification, masked diffusion, and recurrent-depth architectures. v2 adds single-pass recurrent training and up-to-K-fold training-computation savings as main contributions. Its abstract and conclusion emphasize competitive performance across architectures, whereas v1 emphasizes outperforming end-to-end training on its generative tasks.

C2.justification: v2 introduces matching input/output dimensions as an applicability restriction and flags U-Net difficulties, whereas v1 describes U-Nets as ideally suited. It explains the difficulty of ordinary perplexity evaluation and newly acknowledges that concatenated language sequences double sequence memory. It also interprets optimal block count as task-dependent. Conversely, v1's explicit warning about multiplicative autoregressive inference overhead and real-time applicability is removed.

D1.justification: Appendices A–D newly specify numerical EDM defaults, conditioning and attention details, architecture-specific configurations, warmup schedules, and implementation/checkpoint references for added experiments. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. Some existing reproducibility information is lost: v1 explicitly identifies clean-FID, guidance scale 2.0, layer-forward budget matching, and LM1B prompt-length/filtering rules; v2 does not retain those details.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive positioning against stage-specific diffusion experts, recurrent-depth models, and discrete language diffusion. Its NoProp discussion shifts toward architectural transfer and experimentally evaluated comparisons. Meanwhile, v1's survey of deep equilibrium models, synthetic gradients, feedback alignment, and target propagation is dropped. This changes the research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The method becomes a three-step conversion narrative, related work moves before experiments, and experiments are organized by architecture. Appendix material is substantially reorganized, including moving overlap details out of the main method. The title, author list, and document headers also change.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text from two columns to one, redraws the overview, adds conversion and architecture-specific diagrams, and presents training/inference algorithms in comparative panels. The partition plot is updated as Figure 4. Tables gain dataset, metric, and layer-allocation structures, while the overlap table and generated-image/text displays are removed. These are substantial visual changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The explicit conversion recipe, architecture-specific instructions, and masked-diffusion derivation make the framework substantially more actionable. Direct Forward-Forward/NoProp comparisons address v1's reliance on end-to-end baselines, while broader experiments strengthen support for applicability. These gains outweigh losing the overlap sweep, generated examples, and some evaluation specifics. Neither version supplies measured-memory results or confidence intervals, so important limits on the efficiency and performance evidence remain.
